bib.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

question: How can data-parallel training remove its memory redundancy so models of billions to trillions of parameters fit and train efficiently on current GPUs?
hypothesis: Partitioning optimizer states, gradients and parameters across data-parallel ranks (instead of replicating them) gives MP-like memory efficiency with DP-like compute and communication efficiency.
contributions: ZeRO-DP: staged partitioning of optimizer states, gradients and parameters (Pos, Pos+g, Pos+g+p)
ZeRO-R: partitioned activation checkpointing, constant-size buffers, memory defragmentation
Memory and communication analysis showing potential to train over 1T parameters
ZeRO-100B implementation (Pos+g + ZeRO-R) trained 100B+ models with super-linear scaling, and powered Turing-NLG 17B

method.summary: System paper. Analyses where training memory goes (model states 16 bytes/param for mixed-precision Adam, plus residual states) and partitions them across data-parallel ranks. Implements Pos+g plus ZeRO-R as ZeRO-100B in PyTorch and measures throughput and max model size on 400 V100 GPUs against torch DDP and Megatron-LM.
method.task: memory-efficient distributed training of GPT-2-like transformers

datasets.name: not stated (throughput runs); Turing-NLG validation reported on Webtext-103

results.claim: ZeRO-100B trains models up to 170B parameters on 400 V100 GPUs, over 8x larger than Megatron-LM alone.
results.setup: 400 V100 32GB GPUs (25 DGX-2), ZeRO-100B (Pos+g + ZeRO-R) with 16-way MP vs Megatron-LM, GPT-2-like models
results.quote: ZeRO-100B eﬃciently run models with up to 170B parameters on 400 GPUs, more than 8x bigger than Megatron-LM.

results.claim: Sustained aggregate throughput of 15 Petaflops on 400 GPUs for 8B-100B models.
results.setup: 400 V100 GPUs, ZeRO-100B with MP, models 8B to 100B; over 30% of peak
results.quote: ZeRO-100B achieves a sustained throughput of 15 PetaFlops (over 30% of the peak) on average for models with 8B to 100B parameters.

results.claim: ZeRO-100B reaches over 38 TFlops per GPU on a 100B model on 400 GPUs.
results.note: Quote spans a footnote marker in extracted text; same figure at Sec 1 'over 38 TFlops per GPU'
results.quote:
ZeRO runs 100B parameter models on a 400 Nvidia V100 GPU cluster with over
1Prior work [8]

results.claim: Up to 10x speedup over baseline Megatron-LM, largest on large models.
results.setup: Fig 2, per-GPU throughput, ZeRO-100B+MP vs Megatron MP; baseline uses 256-384 GPUs vs 400 for ZeRO
results.note: Baseline given fewer GPUs (lowest power of 2 that fits), which the authors say favours the baseline
results.quote:
ZeRO-100B achieves up to 10x speedup over baseline, signiﬁcantly outperforming on
large models.

results.claim: Super-linear scaling of a 60B model from 64 to 400 GPUs: throughput more than doubles when GPUs double.
results.setup: 60B model, 64 to 400 GPUs, Pos+g, batch per GPU grows as DP degree rises (Table 6)
results.quote:
We observe super linear speedup in the regime of 64-400 GPUs, where the perfor-
mance more than doubles when we double the number of GPUs.

results.claim: ZeRO-100B trains up to 13B parameter models with no MP on 128 GPUs at over 40 TFlops per GPU; plain DP tops out at 1.4B under 20 TFlops.
results.setup: 128 V100 GPUs, DP only, ZeRO-100B vs torch DDP; throughput average
results.quote:
shows that ZeRO-100B can train models with up to 13B parameters without MP on 128 GPUs,
achieving throughput over 40 TFlops per GPU on average.

results.claim: Baseline DDP runs out of memory above 1.4B parameters on 32 GB V100s.
results.quote:
the largest trainable model with DP alone has 1.4B parameters with throughput less than 20 TFlops
per GPU.

results.claim: Mixed-precision Adam needs 16 bytes per parameter (2 fp16 weights + 2 fp16 grads + 12 fp32 optimizer states, K=12); a 1.5B GPT-2 needs at least 24 GB vs 3 GB for fp16 weights.
results.setup: Mixed-precision (fp16/32) Adam, model states only, no activations
results.quote:
In total, this results in 2Ψ + 2Ψ + KΨ = 16Ψ bytes
of memory requirement.

results.claim: Pos cuts model-state memory 4x, Pos+g 8x, Pos+g+p by Nd; e.g. 7.5B model at Nd=64 needs 120 GB (DP), 31.4 GB (Pos), 16.6 GB (Pos+g), 1.88 GB (Pos+g+p).
results.setup: 7.5B model, Nd=64, K=12, per-device model-state memory (analytic)
results.note: Text in Sec 5.3 prints 1.9 GB for the same cell

results.claim: Communication volume: Pos and Pos+g equal baseline DP (2Psi); Pos+g+p is 3Psi, 1.5x baseline.
results.setup: Analytic, per training step, per data-parallel process
results.quote:
The total volume is therefore 3Ψ which is 1.5x compared to the
baseline.

results.claim: Partitioned activation checkpointing cuts checkpoint memory for a 100B model from about 33 GB to about 2 GB per GPU.
results.setup: 100B model, batch 32, seq len 1024, MP 16, one checkpoint per transformer layer (analytic)
results.quote:
it would require about 33 GB of memory per GPU
just to store the activation checkpoints. But with Pa in ZeRO, it can be reduced to about 2 GB
per GPU.

results.claim: Pa communication overhead is under 10% of Megatron MP communication volume.
results.setup: Megatron-LM transformer block with activation checkpointing (analytic)
results.quote:
the total communication overhead of Pa is less than 10% of the original communication volume for model
parallelism.

results.claim: Max model size with ZeRO configs at MP 16, fixed batch: C1 40B, C2 60B, C4 140B, C5 150B.
results.setup: 128 GPUs, MP 16, fixed batch size, Config 5 = Pos+g + CB+MD+Pa+cpu (Table 3, Fig 6/Table 9)
results.note: Text refers to this as Figure 6 but the figure list in text/captions labels differ (Fig 4 'Max model throughput' vs Fig 6 'Max model size'); Table 7 labels it Figure 4
results.quote:
The increase to 150B using C5 is
solely due to further reduction in activation memory from oﬄoading the partitioned activation
checkpoints to the CPU memory.

results.claim: Turing-NLG (17B) trained with ZeRO-100B reached WikiText-103 perplexity 10.21, new SOTA, at 41.4 TFlops/GPU.
results.setup: 17B parameter Turing-NLG, validation perplexity over 300K iterations vs Megatron-LM 8.3B; text says Webtext-103
results.note: Paper prints 'Webtext-103' (probably WikiText-103); throughput 41.4 TFlops/GPU in Sec 10.6
results.quote: It achieved the new SOTA for language models with Webtext-103 perplexity of 10.21.

results.claim: Megatron-LM 40B across two DGX-2 nodes reaches only about 5 TFlops per V100 (under 5% of peak).
results.quote:
We tested a 40B parameter model
using Megatron-LM across two DGX-2 nodes and observe about 5 Tflops per V100 GPU (less
than 5% of hardware peak).

results.claim: A 1T-parameter model on 1024 GPUs holds 16 GB of model state per GPU with Pos+g+p (about 16 TB in total).
results.quote:
16TB divided by 1024 is 16GB, which is well within a reasonable
bound for a GPU (e.g., with 32GB of on-device memory).

results.claim: Training a 1T model would take about 140 days on BERT-Large-equivalent hardware and efficiency, over a year in practice.
results.setup: Back-of-envelope vs Bert-Large 67 min on 1024 GPU DGX-2H; assumes same samples and sequence length
results.quote: training a 1T model would take 140 days, assuming the same hardware and similar computational eﬃciency.

limits: Only Pos+g and ZeRO-R implemented (ZeRO-100B); Pos+g+p (stage 3) and the trillion-parameter claims are analytic, not measured
1T training would take over a year on current hardware; compute gap acknowledged
Baseline given fewer GPUs than ZeRO (256/384 vs 400), which the authors say favours the baseline
No learning rate, optimizer settings, dataset, sequence length or seeds for throughput runs; single measurements without variance
Convergence at large batch is out of scope; authors assert batch size stays small enough
Peak figures are for V100 32GB with NVSwitch; hardware has dated
